candidates.rationale: Paul describes learning to be content in whatever circumstances he finds himself, modeling acceptance of present realities even when they're not ideal.
This verse affirms that there is a season and time for everything, supporting the wisdom of accepting what is appropriate for the current moment rather than forcing perfection.
Paul teaches that godliness with contentment is great gain, and if we have basic necessities, we should be content, embracing sufficiency over perfection.
This proverb advises getting outside work in order first, then building your house—accepting phased progress and provisional steps toward a larger goal.
Jesus teaches about counting the cost before building, implying wisdom in honest assessment of constraints and avoiding overcommitment to unattainable ideals.
